`FETCH_RAISE` refuses, with `FieldFetchBlocked`, a `FieldError` (`django/db/models/fetch_modes.py`, `django/core/exceptions.py:FieldFetchBlocked`).

The notes give the new modes their purposes: the peers bring most cases of the "N+1 queries problem" down to two queries, and the refusal keeps unintended queries out of code where they would cost (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`QuerySet.fetch_mode` sets a mode on a clone of the queryset, which hands it to each instance made from a row through a keyword argument that 6.1 added to `Model.from_db`, `fetch_mode=None` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.fetch_mode`, `django/db/models/base.py:Model.from_db`).

`QuerySet.fetch_mode` sets a mode on a clone of the queryset, which hands it to each instance made from a row through a keyword argument that 6.1 added to `Model.from_db`, `fetch_mode=None` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.fetch_mode`, `django/db/models/base.py:Model.from_db`).

Under the default each sailor's ship was fetched for that sailor, Petrel twice; under the peers the first read fetched the four sailors' ships, by a prefetch of one statement (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.fetch_many`).

In 6.1 a queryset of a model whose own `from_db` accepts neither `fetch_mode=` nor arbitrary keywords crashed when iterated; 6.1.1 made such overrides work again, and deprecated them (`docs/releases/6.1.1.txt`).

At this commit `_get_from_db` inspects the override, warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, and calls it without the mode, so its instances are not given the queryset's (`django/db/models/query.py:_get_from_db`).

The call warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, the notes name `FETCH_PEERS` as the other way to the related objects, and the deprecation timeline has the call raise `TypeError` in Django 2028 (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.select_related`, `docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).

The call warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, the notes name `FETCH_PEERS` as the other way to the related objects, and the deprecation timeline has the call raise `TypeError` in Django 2028 (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.select_related`, `docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).

The notes of 6.1.2, a release expected and not yet made at this commit, list as fixed a bug of 6.1 in which `FETCH_PEERS` did not batch the instances that `select_related` loaded (`docs/releases/6.1.2.txt`).

At this commit each `RelatedPopulator`, which makes the instances of one joined model, keeps a list of peers of its own under a mode that tracks them, so the ships joined to one run of sailors are each other's peers (`django/db/models/query.py:RelatedPopulator`).

Since 6.1 they read the mark that call leaves, `Query.default_ordering` turned off, and use the queryset as it stands (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.first`; [`get`, `first`, `count` and the other methods that run a query at once](../querysets/results.md)).

A queryset made by `QuerySet.union`, `QuerySet.intersection` or `QuerySet.difference` has the model's default ordering since 6.1: `QuerySet._combinator_query` clears the ordering of the combined query and turns its default back on (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._combinator_query`).

The notes give the consequence: where `values` or `values_list` has not selected a field of that ordering, the statement fails with `DatabaseError`, and `order_by()` with no arguments on the combined queryset clears the default (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

The parts were cleared first: each keeps a default ordering of its own, which `order_by()` on the combined queryset leaves in place, and a backend that cannot order the parts of a compound statement, as SQLite cannot, refuses that with another `DatabaseError` (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_combinator_sql`; [Combining querysets: the operators and `union`](../querysets/combining.md)).

`QuerySet.totally_ordered` (6.1) is a property beside `QuerySet.ordered`, true only where the ordering is deterministic (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.totally_ordered`; [Annotations, ordering and the other methods that change the query](../querysets/methods.md)).

Since 5.2 the columns of the statement of `QuerySet.values` and `QuerySet.values_list` stand in the order the names were given; the notes say the order had followed counterintuitive rules that made combining such querysets with `union` unpredictable (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`Query.set_values` records each name, with where its column comes from, in `Query.selected`, and `SQLCompiler.get_select` writes the select list from it (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.set_values`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_select`).

`Query.set_values` records each name, with where its column comes from, in `Query.selected`, and `SQLCompiler.get_select` writes the select list from it (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.set_values`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_select`).
